messages:
jasper: Heads up — staging apply stuck on 'Refreshing state...' for ~6m, terraform sits on module.k8s.kubernetes_service_account.infra-sa

samir: can you paste the last plan output or any error? also make sure there's no remote state lock

jasper: no active lock. `terraform state list` shows the aws and k8s bits out of sync — the k8s SA in state has a different UID than the cluster one. suspect CI re-created the SA during a secret rotation

maria: did we rotate the SOPS secret yesterday? that could trigger a redeploy that recreates SA tokens/annotations

jasper: here's the live SA dump:```kubectl get sa infra-sa -n staging -o yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: infra-sa
  namespace: staging
  uid: 8f4c9b2a-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-abcdef123456
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-staging-infra
```

samir: terraform expects the UID it has in state. usual fix is `terraform import 'module.k8s.kubernetes_service_account.infra-sa' staging/infra-sa` to align state with cluster

jasper: tried import, but apply still hangs during refresh showing the same resource — terraform keeps detecting a diff on the annotation/metadata and the provider appears to loop on get

infra-bot: note: last automated plan ran at 1719502300 via jenkins (lock acquired and released)

maria: check provider versions — we bumped kubernetes provider last week. Sometimes provider schema changes change how UIDs/annotations are compared. `terraform state show` for that SA will help

samir: also try `terraform plan -refresh=false` to generate a plan without doing the refreshing calls, can unblock if you need to push other unrelated changes. but DO NOT apply that to prod blindly

jasper: running `terraform state show module.k8s.kubernetes_service_account.infra-sa` now — state uid differs from cluster one. plan attempts to replace -> refresh waits on kube API

samir: if the import didn't stick, confirm the address you imported into matches the module path exactly. alternatively `terraform state rm` then import the correct current resource. keep a backup of state first

maria: also check apiserver latency/requests — I've seen long GETs cause provider to appear stuck. `TF_LOG=DEBUG` will show which provider call is stalling

jasper: ok doing import with exact address, then re-run plan. if still stuck I'll capture TF_LOG and check apiserver health

jasper: update 1719502715 — import corrected the UID mismatch and a re-run of apply completed. root cause: CI job recreated the SA during a secret rotation window, leaving the old entry in state. action items: add a note in the ops runbook about the rotation ordering, and pin provider versions in the k8s module to avoid schema surprises. :raised_hands:
